witnesses.provenance: Found in Qumran Cave 1; institutional custody and accession are stated by the Israel Museum.
witnesses.rights: Institutional site terms govern images and translation; metadata link only.
witnesses.description: A physical Isaiah witness; its readings are not silently substituted for later editions.

witnesses.title: Codex Sinaiticus
witnesses.repository: British Library; Leipzig University Library; National Library of Russia; Saint Catherine’s Monastery
witnesses.dateNotes: Codex Sinaiticus Project dates the manuscript generally to the fourth century and often the middle of that century.
witnesses.completeness: Earliest complete New Testament; Old Testament portion incomplete
witnesses.provenance: Preserved for centuries at Saint Catherine’s; surviving leaves are now distributed across four partner institutions.
witnesses.rights: Project transcription is CC BY-NC-SA 3.0; manuscript images and repository terms require separate review.
witnesses.description: A multi-work Greek biblical codex with a reunified digital project; work links do not imply a single modern canon or edition.

witnesses.title: Codex Vaticanus
witnesses.dateNotes: Repository and Codex Sinaiticus Project identify it as a fourth-century biblical manuscript.
witnesses.provenance: Repository shelfmark and digital facsimile supplied by the Vatican Library.
witnesses.rights: Vatican Library digital-use terms govern images; IIIF manifest is linked, not copied.
witnesses.description: A distinct fourth-century biblical codex with a verified repository IIIF manifest.

witnesses.title: Codex Alexandrinus, New Testament volume
witnesses.dateNotes: British Library catalogue dates the volume to the fifth century.
witnesses.completeness: One of four codex volumes; this New Testament volume is incomplete
witnesses.provenance: Received by Sir Thomas Roe and given to Charles I in 1627; transferred with the Old Royal Library to the British Museum in 1757.
witnesses.rights: British Library access restrictions and reuse terms apply; metadata only.
witnesses.description: The New Testament volume is linked to its cataloged Gospel contents without claiming the missing leaves survive.

witnesses.title: Nag Hammadi Codex II
witnesses.dateNotes: No normalized date asserted from the collection landing page.
witnesses.provenance: Discovered near Nag Hammadi; collection-level digital documentation is provided by the Claremont Colleges Digital Library.
witnesses.rights: Repository and digital collection terms govern images; metadata link only.
witnesses.description: A multi-work physical codex; individual works and pages remain separately citable.

witnesses.title: Derveni Papyrus
witnesses.dateNotes: UNESCO documentation dates the papyrus between 340 and 320 BCE.
witnesses.provenance: Excavated in 1962 in a documented archaeological context at Derveni.
witnesses.rights: Copyright belongs to the Archaeological Museum of Thessaloniki; metadata and source links only.
witnesses.description: A carbonized physical witness containing ritual discussion and commentary on an Orphic poem.

witnesses.title: P.Oxy. 1, Sayings of Jesus fragment
witnesses.dateNotes: Date requires item-level catalog confirmation and remains unnormalized.
witnesses.provenance: Excavated at Oxyrhynchus and published as the first Oxyrhynchus papyrus; repository-level review remains pending.
witnesses.rights: Oxford repository terms apply; metadata link only.
witnesses.description: A Greek sayings fragment associated with the Gospel of Thomas tradition; association does not make it a complete codex.

witnesses.title: Elephantine Passover Letter
witnesses.repository: Ägyptisches Museum und Papyrussammlung, Staatliche Museen zu Berlin
witnesses.dateNotes: Museum catalog identifies the documentary context; exact normalized year follows the standard 419 BCE identification and should receive curator review.
witnesses.provenance: Excavated at Elephantine by the Royal Museums expedition led by Otto Rubensohn and Friedrich Zucker in the early twentieth century; current custody is documented by the museum.
witnesses.rights: Staatliche Museen zu Berlin terms govern images; metadata link only.
witnesses.description: A documentary witness for calendrical/religious practice, not a scriptural manuscript.

witnesses.title: Mawangdui Laozi silk manuscripts
witnesses.dateNotes: No precise manuscript date normalized from the exhibition overview.
witnesses.completeness: Two early textual witnesses conventionally labeled A and B
witnesses.provenance: Recovered from the Mawangdui Han tomb complex; Hunan Museum documents the silk-manuscript assemblage.
witnesses.rights: Hunan Museum terms govern images; metadata link only.
witnesses.description: Early silk witnesses linked to the received Tao Te Ching tradition without assuming textual identity.

witnesses.title: Guodian Laozi bamboo-slip groups
witnesses.dateNotes: Date remains unnormalized pending an accessible item-level institutional source.
witnesses.provenance: Recovered archaeologically at Guodian; this record preserves the limitation that item-level institutional review remains outstanding.
witnesses.rights: Repository terms govern images; metadata link only.
witnesses.description: Partial bamboo-slip parallels to the received text; they are not described as a complete edition of the Tao Te Ching.

witnesses.title: Library of Congress Gandhara Scroll
witnesses.discoveryLocation: Gandhara region; exact find context not established by catalog
witnesses.dateNotes: Library of Congress dates the scroll roughly between the first century BCE and first century CE.
witnesses.completeness: Approximately 75–80% survives; beginning and end missing
witnesses.provenance: Acquired from a British antiquities dealer in 2003; catalog does not supply a secure excavation context.
witnesses.rights: Library of Congress states public domain or no known copyright restrictions for this collection.
witnesses.description: A digitized early Buddhist scroll with explicit provenance limits and public IIIF image services.

witnesses.title: Gilgit manuscript Lotus Sutra witnesses
witnesses.repository: National Archives of India and Sri Pratap Singh Museum
witnesses.dateNotes: UNESCO dates the collection paleographically to the fifth–sixth centuries CE.
witnesses.completeness: Collection includes canonical and non-canonical works
witnesses.provenance: Discovered in three instalments in the Gilgit region; holdings are divided between two institutions.
witnesses.rights: UNESCO and holding-institution terms apply; metadata link only.
witnesses.description: A manuscript group that includes Lotus Sutra material; no single codex or complete recension is inferred.

witnesses.title: Codex Borgia
witnesses.dateNotes: No date normalized from the digital facsimile landing page.
witnesses.completeness: Complete physical object; interpretive sequence remains debated
witnesses.provenance: Vatican Library shelfmark and digitization establish present custody; earlier provenance requires specialist review.
witnesses.rights: Vatican Library digital-use terms govern images; metadata link only.
witnesses.description: A physical Mesoamerican pictorial manuscript kept distinct from modern interpretations and community authority.

witnesses.title: Codex Laud
witnesses.dateNotes: No date normalized from the digital item record.
witnesses.provenance: Bodleian digital catalog establishes shelfmark and present custody; earlier provenance remains under review.
witnesses.rights: Bodleian Libraries terms govern digital images; metadata link only.
witnesses.description: A physical Mesoamerican manuscript record with no unsupported equation to Codex Borgia.

witnesses.title: Herculaneum Papyrus 118
witnesses.dateNotes: The roll was carbonized by the 79 CE eruption; composition and copying dates remain unnormalized.
witnesses.completeness: Fragmentary roll; work association not asserted
witnesses.provenance: Recovered from the Villa of the Papyri at Herculaneum; Bodleian images are linked through the Herculaneum Society resource guide.
witnesses.rights: Bodleian and project terms govern images; metadata link only.
witnesses.description: A carbonized physical roll from the only surviving ancient Greco-Roman library; Atlas does not infer a work identity from collection membership.
